scenes.title: ROOM ABOVE TWO HUNDRED

publication_copy.headline: ROOM ABOVE TWO HUNDRED
publication_copy.deck: The week the pressure reached everyone
publication_copy.body: Two teams crossed two hundred by Sunday night. One brought a hamburger to a birthday party. The other left his chair and offered a man a bargain on his own mountain. In the Highlands, an outlaw got his laugh, copied a centaur’s stance for a second one, and gave the centaur a reason to chase him. In the east, El Niño’s rain found a way past Red Leopards’ sandbags. Inland, trees were already coming down. Seven Deadly Chins arrived with a jackhammer just as a household settled. Slob on my Dobb kept a delivery appointment in a swamp. Four regular-season games remain. Who has to live with what happened here?

scenes.title: KEEP THE WHOLE LEAGUE IN VIEW

publication_copy.headline: KEEP THE WHOLE LEAGUE IN VIEW
publication_copy.deck: Commissioner’s note • After Week 10
publication_copy.body: There is a difference between being beaten and having to live with the evidence. A score is entered once. A birthday photograph is shown forever. A broken hoop stays broken until someone fixes it. The owner of a swamp still has to watch the next truck drive through. That is the Commonwealth we have spent seasons building, and it is why this league is more than six boxes on a scoreboard. But our stories do not outrank the standings. Nobody is going to Cancún by mathematical decree until the last route is closed. Nobody is healed because a reserve slot looks full. The numbers have settled, and six teams now share 6–4 records. The next week will ask each of us what we have left to field.

The Chili Cheesers makes for it in his good boots.

publication_copy.headline: The Ring Runs Out
publication_copy.deck: The Chili Cheesers vs D0nkey K0ng
publication_copy.body: The Chili Cheesers cuts hard for the service gate. The lasso reaches him before he reaches it. He keeps running for a fraction too long, turning the capture into a skid through the muddy groove he made himself. The crowd's reaction is no longer the sound he came to produce. D0nkey K0ng has not needed the axe. The rope, the arena and The Chili Cheesers’ own decision to flee have done the work.
